row.name: Southeast Slopes from Virginia Lakes
row.description: Leave the parking area cross-country up the southeast slopes, cross low scrub, then slog talus to the broad plateau and the summit. Easy terrain overall but the talus is loose.

row.name: North Ridge
row.overview: A long route along the north ridge of the middle summit of Whorl Mountain. From the notch, scrambling for several hundred feet between Whorl's middle and north summits lead to a squeeze chimney, then the ridge itself gives ten pitches, mostly 50-60 meters each. One way in goes over the North Peak, starting at Matterhorn Pass, with some class 4, then down the ridge and across to the saddle from the west. Protection is scarce at cruxes and the terrain loose, so both climbers must be solid. Some pitches cross exposed knife-edge blocks. Halfway along is the earliest big notch; past it, small towers are bypassed on the west. The rock is gritty; prefer orange rock. Descend the Cl.3-4 SE Chute.
row.approach: Whorl Mountain's north ridge begins at the low point between the middle and north peaks. One way is to scramble up directly from the east, from the hiking bench below. The other is to cross Matterhorn Pass, go up and over the north peak (some class 4 on the summit rocks), pick down the ridge, and traverse into the saddle from the west side. The climb starts from a ledge at the base of a short squeeze chimney.
row.descent_text: The last pitch finishes directly on the summit. Descend by the popular class 3-4 southeast chute, the southeast face route.
